text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Supreme Court by a majority decision upheld President Leghari's November 5 proclamation dissolving the National Assembly and dismissing Benazir Bhutto's government. Bhutto said the verdict was not unexpected but its timing could influence the elections.
- Several supporters of Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party, including women, were injured when police baton-charged them outside the Supreme Court.
- The three P3-C anti-submarine aircraft received by Pakistan from the United States are unfit for making reconnaissance missions, the Defence News in Washington said.
- Pakistan has conveyed its concern to the United States about growing Iranian activities in Afghanistan, Central Asia and the Gulf, a top U.S. military commander said in Washington.
- The government has re-appointed Muhammad Yaqub as Governor of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan for a second term with effect from February 14.
- The executive committee of the National Economic Council approved a Macro Economic Framework and Development Plan worth 708 billion rupees for the next five years.
- The Finance Ministry has finalised a proposal allowing import of reconditioned cars from March.
- The government has allowed import of basic raw materials for the pharmaceutical industry from India to rationalise the prices of medicines.
- State-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd earned revenue of 8.943 billion rupees in the quarter ended December 31, an increase of 782 million rupees over the previous quarter, PTCL said.
- With the receipt of $75 million standby tranche from the International Monetary Fund, Pakistan's liquid foreign exchange reserves are now around $770 million, sources said.
- State-run Pakistan International Airlines is negotiating with Uzbek Airways to acquire three IL-86 aircraft and one TU-154 plane on wet lease.

- The government has approved formation of the Council for Industrial Production under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister to increase local production and reduce imports of defence-related products.
